_comment: Settings for robot_link.py. Change them to match the ASSAR program without touching the code.
_role: server = the robot connects to this PC (URScript socket_open("<PC IP>", port)), the usual UR way. client = this PC connects to the robot or to another program.
_host: server: 0.0.0.0 listens on every network card. client: the IP of the robot or of the other program.
_trigger: Line the robot sends to ask for a move. null = answer every line it sends.
_done_words: Lines from the robot that only say 'finished' and get no answer (they are logged).
_templates: Fields: {cell} 1-9, {index} = cell_map[cell], {row} {col} 0-2, {status}, {message}, {board} (e.g. X../.O./..X), {robot}. URScript socket_read_ascii_float wants numbers in brackets, e.g. "({index})" or "({index},0)".
_cell_map: Our square (1-9, top-left first as seen from the camera) -> the number the robot program expects. Example for 0-8: {"1": 0, ..., "9": 8}.
_level: hard (never loses), easy (sometimes a random move) or random.
_stable_reads: The board must read the same this many times in a row (stable_interval_s apart) before deciding, so a hand still placing a piece is not read. After max_reads without that, the answer is the error template.
